notes: Both supplied 'with's belong to the English predicates that need them to reach their accusatives of material (rules 33, 44); neither noun is an adverbial accusative taking its own preposition.

'new wine' headed on 'new': the ASV writes no bare 'wine' for tirosh in this verse or as its ordinary rendering, so 'wine' is the supplied class noun. Heading on 'wine' as the class noun was the competing reading (rules 8, 31).
